ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and counterparties against the Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the UK HM Treasury Consolidated List. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs, must be identified in accordance with FINTRAC obligations and FATF Recommendation 12; enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval are required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or beneficial-ownership layer identified as opaque.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Registry Electronic System (CORES); NUANS name search is obtained through an authorized Alberta Corporate Registry Agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An Alberta corporate name must contain a distinctive element and an appropriate legal element; the legal element for an unlimited liability corporation must clearly convey unlimited liability by using the prescribed ULC expression. Names may be in English or French, as well as bilingual form, but non-Latin scripts must be transliterated or translated into Latin-alphabet characters acceptable to the Registrar. The Registrar will reject names that are confusingly similar, misdescribe the business, or falsely imply government sponsorship, professional licensing, or regulated status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed for one additional 90-day period by filing a renewal with the Alberta Corporate Registry before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant, through its registry agent, may file a written appeal with the Registrar within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching the original NUANS report, written consents from any holder of a sensitive/professional term, and a comparison showing no material likelihood of confusion. The Registrar issues a written reconsideration decision; a further appeal may be pursued by judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for registration and service-address purposes, provided the virtual office is a physical street address in Alberta and is not a post office box. For an aircraft engine dry-leasing business, a virtual office alone is not sufficient commercial substance and increases the risk of CRA audit, agency, permanent establishment, or general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) recharacterization; substantive decision-making, books and records, and lease administration should be maintained at a real Alberta location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection is low at approximately 1–3% for this non-licensed passive leasing vehicle; however, if CRA or Alberta tax authorities open an audit of cross-border lease flows or ULC loss allocations, the likelihood of premises verification rises to approximately 10–30%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; applicable sections respecting incorporation of unlimited liability corporations, registered office requirements, and officer appointments, including sections 12-21 (incorporation) and Part 1.1 (unlimited liability companies)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine. No escrow account deposit is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: First — That the Corporation issue and allot to the subscriber named in the Subscription Agreement 100 common shares at a price of CAD 1.00, such shares to be fully paid upon acceptance. Second — That the registered office of the Corporation in Alberta be fixed at the address shown in the Certificate of Incorporation, and that the same be maintained with the Alberta Corporate Registry. Third — That [Name] be appointed President, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting. Fourth — That directors and officers are authorized to open banking accounts, execute leases, and take all necessary steps to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request through an approved Alberta corporate name search service or the Alberta Corporate Registry online portal. Confirm the proposed name is distinct and not confusingly similar to an existing entity, including other ULCs and limited liability companies. Pay the applicable name search fee and receive the search report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, amend the proposed legal name and resubmit, or proceed with a numbered Alberta ULC name assigned by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, expressly stating that the corporation is an unlimited liability corporation. Have the incorporating director(s) execute the articles and sign the consent to act as first directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any statutory or internal deficiencies noted by counsel and re-execute the articles before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the executed articles and consents to the Alberta Corporate Registry for registration. Select 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' as the corporate type, pay the applicable filing fee, and await approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice, resubmit the corrected documents within the cure period, or request an administrative correction under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the legal name, registered office, fiscal year end, and unlimited liability designation. Retain certified copies for the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: No additional documents required - internal verification only
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors, apply to the Alberta Corporate Registry for correction under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Alberta ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution. Appoint officers, adopt bylaws, confirm the registered office, and issue share certificates to subscribers.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum or consent formalities are defective, circulate a unanimous director consent pursuant to the ABCA instead of holding a physical meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Alberta and Federal Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number through the CRA Business Registration Online portal. Register the corporation for corporate income tax, and where applicable GST/HST and Alberta corporate tax. Update the registered office address with both authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, request expedited processing from CRA and provide an interim business number if available.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — aircraft engine dry leasing is a commercial leasing activity outside Alberta's industrial licensing regime.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including Business Registration Online, My Business Account, and Represent a Client. Alberta corporate registration is administered separately through the Alberta Corporate Registry; Alberta has no general provincial sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the Alberta unlimited liability corporation through the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain its certificate and corporate identification details. 2. Apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) using Business Registration Online, Form RC1, or an authorized representative process. 3. Register the required CRA program accounts, including GST/HST account RT, corporate income tax account RC, payroll account RP if applicable, and import-export account RM if the entity imports or exports commercial goods. 4. A non-resident-owned corporation must provide its legal name, Canadian registered office, incorporation details, directors, business activities, responsible persons, books-and-records location, and expected Canadian taxable supplies. 5. Canada does not issue a separate VAT identification number; the relevant indirect-tax identifier is the nine-digit BN together with the GST/HST RT account number. 6. The GST/HST registration effective date must be determined under the mandatory registration rules or selected voluntarily, subject to the statutory filing and record-retention obligations. 7. If the corporation conducts commercial import or export transactions, obtain and maintain a CBSA RM account and complete applicable CARM Client Portal onboarding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general check-the-box election that converts an Alberta ULC into a Canadian tax-transparent entity. An Alberta ULC is generally a Canadian corporation subject to Canadian corporate income tax, notwithstanding its unlimited shareholder liability. For United States tax purposes, an eligible Canadian ULC may generally elect its classification under U.S. Treasury Regulations using Form 8832, potentially as disregarded or partnership status depending on ownership. That foreign election does not change Canadian tax treatment and may create cross-border hybrid-entity, treaty, foreign tax credit, limitation-on-benefits, or hybrid-mismatch consequences. Canadian corporate tax elections may apply to specific transactions, but they are not entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), administered federally under the Excise Tax Act. Alberta has no general provincial sales tax. Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applies only in participating provinces and is not applicable solely because the entity is located in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, excluding supplies of financial services and certain other excluded amounts, measured under the small-supplier rules over a single calendar quarter or the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Registration can be voluntary before the threshold is exceeded. A non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada may be required to register even if the ordinary small-supplier threshold is not met, depending on the applicable place-of-supply and carrying-on-business facts.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general real-time electronic-invoice clearance, mandatory government e-invoicing network, or universal digital tax-stamping requirement for GST. Commercial invoices and GST invoices may be electronic if they contain the prescribed information, including supplier identity and BN, invoice date, recipient details where required, description, consideration, GST rate, GST amount, and applicable registration references. GST/HST returns and related payments are filed through CRA electronic services, including GST/HST NETFILE or other mandated electronic channels where applicable. Commercial import and export declarations are processed through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) CARM Client Portal and applicable electronic reporting systems, including the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods may generally be zero-rated where the goods are exported from Canada under the Excise Tax Act and the supplier retains evidence that the goods were shipped or delivered outside Canada and were not used, consumed, or supplied in Canada before export, subject to statutory exceptions. A supply of services to a non-resident may be zero-rated only where the service falls within the statutory non-resident-service rules and is not excluded by the place-of-supply provisions. Dry leasing of aircraft engines is not automatically zero-rated merely because the lessee is non-resident or the payment is received offshore. The GST result depends on the location and delivery of the engine, possession or use in Canada, lease characterization, lessee status, export timing, aircraft qualification, and the specific zero-rating provisions for aircraft, aircraft parts, and related services. Where a leased engine remains in Canada or is used in Canada, GST may generally apply unless a specific relieving rule applies. The lessor must retain contracts, delivery and export evidence, engine serial-number records, lessee residency and use certifications, transport records, customs records, payment evidence, and proof supporting the applicable zero-rating provision. Input tax credits and any GST rebate or refund claim require valid documentary support and must be claimed within the applicable statutory limitation periods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) export declaration or other CBSA-approved export reporting record, where required
Commercial invoice or lease-related commercial documentation identifying the supplier, lessee, engine description, serial number, value or consideration, destination, and transaction terms
Air waybill, bill of lading, cargo control document, delivery receipt, or equivalent carrier evidence showing movement outside Canada
Transport, handover, and destination records establishing the date and place of export and absence of Canadian use before export where relevant
Customs release, temporary-export, re-export, or other applicable customs records
Executed lease, delivery, acceptance, insurance, maintenance, and return-condition documents
Evidence of non-resident status and business use, together with records establishing the statutory basis for zero-rating

Bank payment or remittance records where commercially available; an inward remittance certificate is not a general mandatory Canadian GST document and Canada has no general foreign-exchange repatriation certificate requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. CRA may reassess GST that was incorrectly treated as zero-rated, impose applicable interest from the statutory due date, deny related input tax credits or rebates, and assess penalties for failure to remit, false statements, repeated failures, or gross negligence. The gross-negligence penalty can generally be 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed credit, subject to the applicable statutory calculation. False or deceptive documentation may also create civil and criminal exposure, including prosecution under the Excise Tax Act or Criminal Code. CBSA may impose administrative monetary penalties for inaccurate or late export reporting and may pursue customs enforcement remedies. There is no single fixed export-zero-rating clawback period or penalty; reassessment periods, interest, penalty amounts, and enforcement consequences depend on the transaction, conduct, records, and applicable statutory provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority) and Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) (banking supervision); FINTRAC (anti-money-laundering and cross-border funds transfer reporting); Global Affairs Canada and Finance Canada for sanctions and international financial policy. Canada does not operate a dedicated foreign-exchange control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. There are no general exchange controls, no repatriation permits, and no mandatory conversion rates. Non-residents may freely convert CAD to foreign currency and remit income, dividends, interest, and lease rentals after fulfilling tax withholding and FINTRAC reporting obligations. Dividend and interest distributions from a Canadian ULC to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (typically 25% absent treaty relief, reducible under applicable tax treaties). Aircraft-engine dry-leasing receipts are current-account rental income and are freely remittable. Practical constraints arise only from bank AML/KYC procedures and the requirement to provide accurate wire purpose codes and supporting leasing documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandated conversion ratio in Canada. Export receipts, including engine lease rental payments received in foreign currency, may be retained, converted, or used offshore at the exporter's discretion. However, all cross-border electronic funds transfers and cash transactions of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and financial institutions must maintain sufficient audit trails. Export documentation and lease invoices must support the payment narrative for AML and tax-revenue reconciliation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low. Foreign fintech e-money institutions (EMIs) and digital payment service providers are not regulated as banks in Canada and cannot accept deposits in the ordinary course of a Canadian corporation's treasury operations. They may only operate as money services businesses (MSBs) or foreign money services businesses if registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and they generally lack direct access to the Canadian high-value payment system (Lynx). Such entities are best used as auxiliary collection/currency-conversion tools only, not as primary treasury accounts for a ULC engaged in cross-border aircraft-engine leasing. Legal constraints include compliance with Canadian banking law, Canadian sanctions, and FATF transparency requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Alberta or federal statute explicitly requires directors to appear physically at a bank branch to open a corporate bank account. Schedule I Canadian banks typically require at least one director, officer, or authorized signatory to complete a due-diligence interview and sign the account mandate. In practice, most Tier-1 banks permit remote/electronic onboarding through video conference and digital e-signatures for Canadian corporations where beneficial ownership is transparent and the entity maintains a registered office in Alberta. Enhanced due diligence may require an in-person meeting where the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident, the entity is unregulated, or the transaction profile involves high-value aviation assets. A ULC's unlimited liability structure and possible non-resident shareholder register will increase scrutiny, but remote opening remains feasible subject to the bank's internal KYC risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership or corporate opacity of the Alberta ULC structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed Article of Incorporation/Registration, Alberta corporate record from the Corporate Registry including registered office address, corporate minute book and organizational resolutions, a copy of the ULC's unanimous shareholder agreement, the register of individuals with significant control (as required under Alberta law), a current certificate of incumbency, and notarized identification and proof-of-address for all directors and beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk aviation asset profile and cross-border dry-leasing structure involving aircraft engines
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master aircraft-engine dry-lease agreements, corresponding lease payment schedule and invoices, aircraft-engine registration or maintenance tracking documentation, engine maintenance/return condition log, independent valuation or appraiser's report, insurance certificate and aviation liability coverage, and a clearly documented chain of lease/ownership preventing suspected sanctions evasion or aviation financing fraud.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder participation and expected inbound/outbound high-value wire transfers without a clear economic purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residency certificates of all non-resident shareholders and beneficial owners, relevant tax treaty positions (e.g., Form W-8BEN-E for US parties or equivalent), a board resolution authorizing the treasury structure and wire-transfer delegation, a business plan showing lease-rental routing, underlying transaction contracts, source-of-wealth evidence for injected capital, and three years of projected cash flow identifying expected counterparties and settlement rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Currency-conversion and hedging activity flagged as potential money laundering or unregulated financial activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written treasury and ALM policy, derivative master agreements (ISDA/CEDA or bank's standard FX terms) with a regulated Canadian bank, confirmed hedging mandate and pricing evidence, bank account statements showing clear cash-flow mapping to lease receivables and operating expenses, and copies of all FINTRAC large-transaction and cross-border electronic funds transfer reports where triggered.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from shareholders into the Alberta ULC should be routed by SWIFT wire transfer to the ULC's Tier-1 bank account in Canada using a compliant payment narrative. The wire message should clearly identify the beneficiary as the ULC, reference the capital contribution purpose (e.g., 'shareholder loan subordination' or 'paid-in capital'), and provide the source-of-funds details. Canada has no exchange-control approval requirement, but the receiving bank will require a completed 'Purpose of Transfer' disclosure for regulatory reporting and tax reconciliation. Where the parent/shareholder is non-resident, the transfer should be documented under a signed subscription agreement, board resolution, or shareholder loan agreement to support the Philippines? No, Canada's tax analysis. Use 'source-of-wealth declaration', evidence of bank guarantee, and the required FINTRAC cross-border EFT report threshold. The bank may require a preliminary account-activity questionnaire and cash-flow forecast before accepting the capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements for the aircraft-engine leasing business (maintenance, insurance, engine procurement, lessee refunds, security deposits, and professional fees) should be executed via SWIFT MT103 in USD/EUR (through correspondent bank) or through Canada's high-value payment system Lynx (formerly LVTS) for CAD-denominated payments. For major transactions and security deposits, a commercial letter of credit (documentary LC) may be used if the supply or lease obligation requires seller/lessee protection, but dry-leasing rental payments are ordinarily settled by clean telegraphic transfer (MT103) rather than an LC. Each outbound transfer must be supported by the relevant lease contract, invoice, or vendor agreement; the remitter must provide the appropriate transaction narrative and, where applicable, use the corresponding ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., 'BUSE' for business services, 'LEAS' for leasing, or 'INTR' for interest). Bank-imposed sanctions screening and OFAC/SAR obligations must be satisfied before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank or an OSFI-regulated dealer
Outright FX forwards up to 12 months tenor for CAD/USD lease-rental flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the underlying currency is illiquid or the bank requires a deliverable alternative in a defined onshore market currency
Cross-currency swaps matching long-term engine lease receivables and debt-service liabilities
FX options (call/put) as permitted under the bank's derivatives documentation and internal risk policies

stage_5.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Rules regarding annual confirmation for shareholding transfers
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
